title: GBRG Supply-Chain Graph-Signal Map (declared)
description: DECLARED mapping from real gbrg-analyze BlastRadiusProofArtifact graph signals (over the HellGraph blast-radius topology) to the six inherent-risk factors and the four common-mode cluster components consumed by gbrg.governance.supply_chain_risk. This is the LIVE-scoring counterpart to supply-chain-risk-weights.v0.json: the weights say how factors combine, THIS file says how each factor is DERIVED from an observed graph signal — so the scorer runs over real topology instead of hand-supplied dicts. Numbers are DATA, never magic numbers in code: gbrg.governance.supply_chain_pipeline loads THIS file. A factor the code graph cannot observe (execution/publishing authority) is marked observable:false and derived from a declared conservative (fail-closed) prior plus real source-locator path signals, never fabricated as a measurement.

provenance.derived_from: gbrg-analyze --emit-edges BlastRadiusProofArtifact + CALLS/IMPORTS/TESTED_BY edges over real gbrg crate topology

inherent_factor_derivation.description: Each of the six declared inherent factors (K,P,E,O,C,V of supply-chain-risk-weights.v0.json) is derived from an observed BlastRadiusProofArtifact signal. `observable:true` factors are read directly off the frozen-index graph; `observable:false` factors are not visible in a code-call graph and use a declared conservative prior raised only by real path signals on the cell's source locator (fail-closed, and recorded as a PRIOR in the derivation string).

criticality_K.rationale: blast_radius (0..1) already models downstream business impact if the cell fails/is compromised — the estate's own criticality signal.

concentration_C.rationale: high in-degree hub = single point of failure / weak alternatives. Saturation 15 = the analyzer's own bounded dependents threshold; dependents_count/15 clamped to 1.

velocity_V.rationale: historical change rate (per day). Saturation 0.5/day marks sustained churn as maximal operational instability.

opacity_O.rationale: lack of test evidence + weak epistemic grounding = low graph visibility / attestation. Combines an untested component with an epistemicLevel opacity scale; the two weights sum to 1.

execution_E.rationale: capability to run code during install/build/runtime is NOT observable from a function-call graph. A moderate fail-closed prior is used; machine-generated cells are raised (codegen runs at build); real source-locator path signals raise it further. Never emitted as a measurement.

path_signals.note: cargo build script executes at build time
CI / helper scripts run in the pipeline
workflow definitions execute privileged CI steps

privilege_P.rationale: publish/sign/administer authority is NOT observable from a function-call graph. A fail-closed prior is used, raised only by real source-locator path signals. Never emitted as a measurement.

path_signals.note: publishing / signing / credential surfaces carry high authority

cluster_common_mode_derivation.description: The four declared common-mode cluster components (cluster_common_mode_weights of supply-chain-risk-weights.v0.json) are derived from an aggregate over the cluster's member artifacts. Provider `shares` for the normalized HHI are the members' dependents_count normalized to sum 1 (a node carrying more of the cluster's dependents is a larger 'provider').

hhi_normalized_concentration.rationale: concentration of the cluster's dependent load across its member nodes (Herfindahl-Hirschman, normalized 0..1).

blast_radius.rationale: cluster blast = worst-case member blast_radius (how many critical services the cluster can take down).

time_to_recover.rationale: fraction of members with NO test path proxies how hard the cluster is to restore/verify after failure.

exit_difficulty.rationale: mean member opacity proxies how hard the cluster is to substitute, mirror, or contractually exit.

derived_kri_kci.description: KRI/KCI metrics that are GENUINELY computable from the graph corpus (feeding gbrg.governance.supply_chain_risk.evaluate_kri against supply-chain-risk-weights.v0.json thresholds). Only these are auto-derived; every other indicator must come from an external evidence source and is otherwise left unevaluated (never silently passed).

KCI02.metric: Critical dependencies with SBOM and graph visibility
